adjudicated_statement: Work over C with Q-coefficients. Let g>=2 and n>=2. Let pi:C->M_g be the universal closed curve of genus g, and let C^n be its n-fold fibre product over M_g, a smooth separated finite-type Deligne-Mumford stack. Identify M_{g,n} with the open complement in C^n of the union of pairwise diagonals. Then, for every integer k, restriction along this open immersion is a morphism of mixed Hodge structures inducing a surjection W_k H^k(C^n;Q) ->> W_k H^k(M_{g,n};Q). The surjection follows from Deligne, Theorie de Hodge II, Corollaire 3.2.17: for a smooth separated scheme (and, with Q-coefficients, a smooth finite-type Deligne-Mumford stack via a scheme atlas), W_k H^k equals the image of H^k of any smooth proper compactification; a smooth proper compactification of C^n is simultaneously a compactification of the open M_{g,n}, so both lowest-weight groups equal the image of the same compactification cohomology and restriction factors that image. Consequently W_k H^k(M_{g,n};Q) is a quotient of W_k H^k(C^n;Q), and any generation, vanishing, or Tate-type upper bound on the source yields the same upper bound on the target. Identifying the kernel of restriction on W_k, including Gysin exactness for the diagonal divisors and the symplectic Schur-Weyl or traceless decomposition of (R^1 pi_* Q)^{tensor n}, is needed only to upgrade the surjection to an isomorphism (Canning-Larson-Payne Lemma 3.1(a)). This surjection does not assert that Kunneth summands of H^*(C^n) are summands of R^* f_* Q for the non-proper map f:M_{g,n}->M_g; that identification remains invalid, because the fibres are configuration spaces of distinct points and R^1 of the punctured curve is mixed of weights 1 and 2. In particular the statement applies at the campaign case (g,n,k)=(6,6,26).
contradiction_resolution: No claim-level contradiction: contradicts_claim_ids is empty and the statement does not oppose CONJ-0001, THM-0001 through THM-0007, OBS-0001, or RED-0001. It is compatible with THM-0001 (smooth proper stacks have pure weight-k cohomology, used on a compactification) and with corroborated FND-0020/FND-0037 (the route uses the closed universal curve, whose R^1 is pure of weight 1, not the mixed punctured R^1). It is distinct from FND-0048 (image of H^{26}(Mbar_{6,6}) rather than of W_{26}H^{26}(C^6)), FND-0030 (Borel-Moore dual of top-weight compact support), and FND-0165 (compact-support corner injection); do not merge. Local contested passage in ATT-0135 Section 1: the open inclusion M_{g,n}->C^n induces a surjection on lowest weight W_k in degree k because, after a common smooth normal-crossings compactification, W_k of either smooth open is the image of compactification cohomology and restriction factors that image. REV-0184 independently accepted that surjection and recorded that only the containment direction is load-bearing downstream at (6,6,26), because H^{20}(M_6;V^{tensor 6}) vanishes by vcd, so symplectic Schur-Weyl is decorative for the submitted theorem. Primary checks: Deligne, Theorie de Hodge II, Publ. Math. IHES 40 (1971), (3.2.16) and Corollaire (3.2.17) (NUMDAM PDF, journal pp. 39-40) identify W_n H^n(X;Q) of a smooth separated scheme X with the image of H^n of any smooth proper compactification; a compactification of C^n is simultaneously a compactification of the open M_{g,n}, so restriction of that common image is surjective on W_k. Canning-Larson-Payne, arXiv:2307.08830v3, Lemma 3.1 proof, first sentence, states the same surjection for the stack inclusion M_{g,n} subset C^n and uses diagonal classes Delta_{ij} only later to identify the kernel for the isomorphism. The original candidate wording is corrected: an upper bound on the target is a quotient bound via the surjection, not a claim that nothing else is ever needed; the stack setting is licensed by the published CLP statement; Kunneth of the proper map C^n->M_g is not Leray of the non-proper map M_{g,n}->M_g. Promote from candidate to corroborated. Merge target: none.
